newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge searches offices of Chirac ally.
newsitem.headline: French judge searches offices of Chirac ally.

text.p: A French judge probing suspected graft over public works contracts searched the offices of the Paris regional council headed by an ally of President Jacques Chirac, justice sources said on Thursday.
Judge Armand Riberolles led a search of the Ile de France council which is headed by Michel Giraud, a senior member of Chirac's Gaullist RPR party.
"It's a logical step of the investigation, I have nothing to hide," Giraud told reporters after the search.

The council was placed under investigation on suspicion of favouritism, fraud, forgery and anti-competitive practices in public tenders earlier this month, just two days after the Left swept to power in a snap parliamentary election on June 1.
The investigation targeted "persons unknown", a legal device enabling a magistrate to determine who, if anyone, should be brought to trial for suspected offences.
The Left accused Chirac of calling the election almost 10 months early to pre-empt mounting scandals involving kickbacks on public building contracts going into his party's coffers.
The Greens group in the regional council complained last year that Giraud's council had awarded a string of contracts to a single consultancy firm, Patrimoine Ingenierie, from 1989-94.
It said 171 of 212 such consultancy contracts went to the company, worth a total of 319.5 million francs ($54 million).
